correctness.rationale: The bivariate polynomial is the reduced weighted Laplacian determinant with explicitly computed two zero-sum eigenspaces and a two-dimensional residual block. Coefficient algebra proves the conditional endpoint identities, with strict opposite directions when sizes differ. The covariance polynomial has a unique positive root. The independent Prüfer and Bareiss exact checker passed 250 assertions. No infinite extrapolation from finite tests is needed.

evidence: The marked vertex degree is a local edge-incidence statistic, while the bridge count is an entire cut-size statistic.

A general joint edge-event theorem could recover the bivariate polynomial after specialization, but the sharp conditional nonmonotonicity and covariance reversal were not found as stated results.

originality.rationale: The exact joint bridge-count/marked-degree polynomial, universal nonmonotone conditional regression when community sizes differ, and unique covariance reversal were not identified as direct statements or implied explicit classifications in inspected primary literature or published-record comparisons. Prior general Gibbs spanning-tree moment methods and UST degree laws are credited. Priority remains subject to older multitype spanning-tree enumeration checks.
residual_risks: A multitype Cayley-tree enumerator or general transfer-current result may already yield the same specialized regression theorem after a nontrivial coefficient calculation.
Literature indexing and unpublished results are incomplete; no independence or exhaustive novelty certificate is claimed.

value.rationale: Two natural observables on a weighted community network—the local vertex degree and intercommunity bridge count—have a robust all-size conditional nonmonotonicity, even as the marginal covariance is tuned through a single sharp conductance threshold. The entire finite-size distribution is explicitly available and the balanced symmetry case distinguishes mean independence from full independence.
